meta.commitMessage:
feat(cli): the ledger read verbs — story, cards, floating, account, jobs, outbox, burst, posture (v2 CLI plan, phase 02) (#1311)

Eight tenant-scoped read views behind `/api/v1/ops/...` (fork F6, one file
for the operator surface), admitted to tokens: a story's whole timeline
(audit rows incl. the cli_command rows, every container permit with its url
variant and Meta's answer, its cards); a story's cards on every binding,
adopted twins included; what is floating (approved with a debit) with the
job that retries it — or the failed one, the failure `--watch` exits 6 on;
an account against its cap today; the job queue by kind × lane × state
with failed samples; what is still owed or lost on the chats; a burst as
one timeline (taps, permits, float waits, siblings, review cards, outcomes);
and the database's posture (the runner's ledger under the runner's own
grant — F7 — the connected role, every tenant table's RLS state, the
SECURITY DEFINER doors).

Every view is one bounded statement with an explicit workspace_id
predicate on every table, and every row carries the table's own
workspace_id rather than a stamp from the parameter; rate_counters and the
system jobs, both outside RLS, are never read. The gate seeds two
workspaces through the API and proves every view three ways — as
svc_ingress under the policies, by route scope (a readonly token, a
session, a service identity for its own workspace; a stranger 404, a
foreign identity wrong_workspace), and as a role that bypasses RLS, so the
predicates confine the rows, not the policies — and proves posture's RLS
drift and each ledger state live. One window grammar in the vocabulary
module serves the API's `since` and the CLI's `--since`: Nm|Nh|Nd, an
ISO-8601 timestamp (naive = UTC) or a bare date, thirty days at most,
never in the future, an overflow refused (422 / usage 64). Jobs and outbox
rows still owed are listed at any age; the finished ones are windowed.

The CLI: `storydump story|cards|floating|account|jobs|outbox|burst|posture`,
every workspace the token can read or `--workspace <id or name>`, one
envelope shape (`data.workspaces[].rows`), `--watch [--every N]` printing
only changes with the first read as the baseline (exit 0 on the terminal
condition, 6 on a failure that arrives, Ctrl-C 0), the CLI's own
sentences. The guide documentation/operations/reading-the-ledger.md
replaces the SQL recipes.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

meta.commitMessage:
feat(auth): API tokens as the second credential, and the storydump CLI (v2 CLI plan, phase 01) (#1310)

Tokens as principals. A bearer value with the `sdt_` prefix is an API token
and resolves through `service_tokens.resolve`; every other bearer value and
the cookie stay on the session path byte for byte. Two principal kinds on
one table (077 `service_tokens.user_id` + `ck_service_token_subject`, `07`
§23): a person-bound token acts as its person across their memberships,
never above the membership role, over the `cli` channel, with one direct
`cli_command` audit row (token id + name, the idempotency reference)
beside the port's own transition row; a workspace service identity reads
its one workspace and never writes (F10). Tokens are admitted to
`TOKEN_ROUTES` only (`/me/principal`, own-token list/revoke, the command
route); every other route depends on `require_session` and refuses a token
with `reason: session_required`. A revoked, expired or unknown token and a
disabled person's token answer 401 without saying which; a live token asking
for what it may not have answers 403 with its reason.

Minting is a session's act on the web: Settings › API tokens (personal
tokens; workspace service identities for admins and owners, role forced
readonly), the secret shown once with a copy control, list, revoke — BFF
routes under /api/me/tokens and /api/workspaces/{id}/tokens.

The `storydump` CLI (`pip install -e '.[cli]'`): login (secret from the
prompt or stdin; OS keychain by default, failing closed; a 0600 file by
--insecure-storage; STORYDUMP_TOKEN overrides — F2 (d)), logout, whoami,
tokens list|revoke; --json envelopes; exit codes 0/1/2/3/4/64; redaction.
It imports nothing from `src` but the new vocabulary module, which owns the
closed sets, the envelope, the exit codes and the CLI's sentences (the
command port re-exports VOCABULARY and REASONS).

The migration runner grants SELECT on its own ledger to svc_ingress where
it creates the ledger (F7 (c)) — outside the advertised stream, which the
gates replay into a database with no runner schema.

Tests: units for the service, the principal, the routes, the vocabulary,
the storage backends, the client, the output and the entry point; the gate
`tests/scripts/test_service_tokens_gate.py` drives the real app as
svc_ingress end to end; the runner's grant gate; the web's lib, route and
tab tests; the mutation battery tests/mutations/cli_v2_01.sh.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
